assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and the Jarzynski equality turned the second law into exact statements about work and entropy production in small, driven, far-from-equilibrium systems. The idea is original, conceptually clean and has become a standard tool in stochastic thermodynamics, single-molecule biophysics and nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, a field close to my own work on stochastic dynamics.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are the Evans-Searles and related transient fluctuation relations and Jarzynski's nonequilibrium work relation; Crooks's detailed fluctuation theorem sharpened them. The credited list omits other early figures (for example Gallavotti and Cohen, as I recall), so the credit is genuinely contested. Jarzynski and Evans give a defensible two-person core, but I am not certain this is the fairest split.
assessment.maturity: Mature: experimentally verified from RNA-hairpin pulling and colloidal-particle experiments through to quantum systems, and stable for roughly three decades. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among Evans, Cohen, Gallavotti, Searles, Jarzynski and Crooks is disputed and I have not independently verified the details.
Some committee members may judge it more a theoretical framework than a discovery of a physical phenomenon.
Whether the experimental tests probe the relations beyond what ordinary thermodynamics already implies is a fair question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is an exact-in-infinite-dimensions treatment of strongly correlated electrons that made the Mott transition and correlated-metal physics quantitatively tractable. It is a statistical-physics idea with very wide lasting impact, and combined with electronic-structure methods (DFT+DMFT) it is used for real materials.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit, and Georges and Kotliar established the mapping to a self-consistent quantum impurity problem. Vollhardt, Georges and Kotliar form a natural trio, but Metzner's role (I recall that he is a co-originator) is not in the supplied credited names, so the credit is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with more than thirty years of applications and benchmarking against cold-atom simulators and numerical methods. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: The omission of Walter Metzner from the credited names leaves an unresolved allocation question.
Predictive success for real materials depends on approximations in the DFT+DMFT step, and the theory is not exact in finite dimensions.
The work is theory-led, and the committee has sometimes favoured clear experimental discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a conceptually new view of intracellular organization, with a clear physical-chemistry and soft-matter basis. It connects polymer physics and nonequilibrium active-droplet theory to biology, and the field has grown very large.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman showed that P granules behave as liquid droplets, and Jülicher supplied the physical theory of active droplets and phase separation in cells. This is a plausible three-person physics configuration. Others (for example Rosen, Pappu and Eisenberg-type contributors, as I recall) have a claim, and the biological significance may favour a different prize.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature, with a decade of independent confirmation. Debate continues over which condensates are truly liquid-like or functional, so the interpretation is still settling.
uncertainties: It is unclear whether the physics community or the chemistry and medicine communities would be expected to recognize it.
The functional relevance of many reported condensates in vivo is debated and the generality of the phase-separation interpretation is not settled.
Attribution is spread across a larger community than three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution is a foundational application of quantum information, with a clear physical principle (no-cloning and measurement disturbance) and deployed implementations. It follows naturally from the recent recognition of quantum entanglement and Bell tests.
assessment.attribution: BB84 (Bennett and Brassard) and the entanglement-based protocol (Ekert) are the conceptual core. Jian-Wei Pan's work on satellite-based networks is an engineering and experimental achievement of great scale, which fits a different kind of recognition and would make a fourth credited person unavailable under the three-laureate limit. The three theory names are the cleanest conceptual set.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are over forty years old and have extensive experimental demonstrations. Practical security against side-channel attacks and the commercial role remain open, so the recognition looks timely for the principle but less so for the networks.
uncertainties: Whether this is physics rather than computer science or cryptography is a judgement call.
Excluding Pan leaves a large experimental contribution unrecognized.
Practical security of real devices is not a settled matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and of topological insulators established a new class of phases with protected edge and surface states, a major conceptual and experimental development in condensed matter physics that follows the topological line of earlier prizes.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 quantum spin Hall insulator; Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not among the credited names here. Hasan's work on 3D topological insulators is a further strong claim. A three-person grouping inevitably leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature and extensively confirmed in multiple materials, and widely taught. Timely, perhaps somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Credit is split across theory (Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents) and experiment (Molenkamp, Hasan and others), and no three names capture it cleanly.
The two topological-insulator ballot entries overlap, so recognizing one would pre-empt the other.
I did not verify the details of who had priority on three-dimensional topological insulators.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters and have made quantum simulation of many-body phases an experimental reality. The superfluid to Mott-insulator transition and the single-site-resolved microscopes are clear and lasting results, directly relevant to statistical physics of interacting systems.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch and Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard realization, Greiner, Bloch and colleagues observed the Mott transition, and Greiner's quantum-gas microscope showed single-atom resolution. Cirac also has a claim and Hänsch's group is also associated with the early work, so a three-person set is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than twenty years of independent confirmation across many groups. The simulation programme continues to develop, which suggests the most significant results may still be coming.
uncertainties: Credit is spread across many experimental groups and the theory proposals.
Whether the main achievement is the Mott observation, the microscope or the general quantum-simulation concept is not resolved.
The Bose-Einstein condensation prize of 2001 may make some members see this as incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics is the architecture on which superconducting quantum processors are built, giving strong coupling of artificial atoms to microwave photons and enabling dispersive readout and gate operations. It is a concrete and influential invention with a clear physical basis.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues made the theoretical proposal, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. This is a relatively clean theory-plus-experiment triplet, though Devoret and others also made major contributions to superconducting circuits, as I recall, and the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits overlaps in subject.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with two decades of confirmation and widespread use. The recent prize in related work may argue for waiting, though it also shows the committee's interest in the area.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent prize and with trapped-ion and other quantum computing entries could affect balance among laureates.
Whether the committee views this as an enabling technology or a fundamental discovery is a judgement call.
I am not certain about the full priority history of the 2004 proposal and demonstration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened the field of moire quantum materials by predicting flat bands and then revealing correlated insulators and superconductivity at tunable carrier density. It is a striking and original idea with large impact and a rich set of connections to strongly correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat bands in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero's group observed the correlated and superconducting states in 2018. This is a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration, although Cao and other co-authors of the experiment are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Relatively young: the central observations date from 2018 and the interpretation of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still being worked out. Confirmation of the phenomenology is solid, but the underlying mechanism is not settled, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is not established.
Reproducibility and sample-dependence issues were noted in the early years and have only partly resolved.
The prize may be better deferred until the field's interpretation stabilizes.
